FMS Avanti 90 mm — source concept brief

1. Intent and configuration summary

Model the FMS 90 mm Avanti 18th Anniversary EDF sport jet that carried the recorded Aleph flight stack. The source geometry follows the production FMS airframe rather than the BDX turbine-jet model. The user-provided flown configuration is authoritative for total mass and longitudinal CG:

  • total ready-to-fly mass: 7.72 lb = 3.501733 kg;
  • CG: 2.75 ft = 0.8382 m aft of the nose tip.

The concept is an autonomous, image-grounded, source-locked reproduction. Published dimensions anchor absolute scale; catalog views provide shape ratios; the manual and component listings provide propulsion and control facts. It is not a scan-grounded reproduction, so every image-derived value retains a nonzero tolerance and the aerodynamic, structural, and propulsion uncertainties remain explicit below.

Configuration: 90 mm 12-blade electric ducted fan, conventional swept wing with separate flaps and ailerons, conventional horizontal tail with split elevators, one centerline vertical tail and rudder, retractable tricycle gear, and no thrust-vectoring tail.

The three catalog sources are FMS product images served by the Monkey Hobby FMS150PRD listing. Their original URLs are embedded as PNG text metadata in the canonical sketches. The side and front views include deployed landing gear; gear pixels were retained as source evidence but excluded from body measurements.

PNG conversion record:

  • EXIF orientation was applied by Pillow on load; the PNG sources carried no orientation transform.
  • All views were converted to RGB and cropped to the aircraft.
  • The catalog top view measured span/length ≈0.902 although the two published anchors require 1.290/1.360 = 0.948529. It was globally widened from 690 to 726 px while retaining 765 px length (1.0522× horizontal correction).
  • The side and front views were cropped without anisotropic correction.
  • All outputs have the PNG signature 89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A.

The user mass on the published 0.320 m² area gives 109.4 g/dm² wing loading. At the 30 m/s reference condition, level-flight CL is approximately 0.195. The retained physical database reaches 30.529 m/s maximum GNSS ground speed, so 30 m/s is a condition anchor, not a claim of measured true airspeed.

4. Coordinate, scale, and rectification method

Open-air geometry uses x = 0 at the nose tip, positive aft; y = 0 on the symmetry plane, positive right; z = 0 at the nose-tip center, positive up.

  • Top view: near-orthographic catalog image, cropped and globally widened 1.0522× to satisfy both published span and length. After correction the nominal scale is 1.778 mm/px in both axes. No four-point controls or grid were available.
  • Side view: catalog profile, cropped but not projectively rectified. Nose to tail is about 747 source pixels, or 1.82 mm/px. The finite wing/tail depth and deployed gear make it a profile reference, not a precision drawing.
  • Front view: catalog front photo. Published span sets approximately 1.82 mm/px at the wing plane. Perspective makes the aft fin and horizontal tail too small for direct scaling; they are cross-checks only.

Image coordinates were read to the visible outer foam boundary, excluding shadows, gear and control horns. Product-image antialiasing and residual perspective justify the nonzero tolerances below.

5. Measurement and inference record

Main-wing planform

The manual's page-4 wing component is the strongest planform evidence. Its 230 px span, 61.37 px mean root chord, 27.04 px effective tip chord and 31.93 px leading-edge setback give taper 0.4406. Scaling the trace by both the published span and area agrees to 0.05%, unlike the perspective catalog view:

root chord = 2 S / [b (1 + taper)] = 0.3444 m
tip chord  = taper × root chord       = 0.1517 m
LE sweep   = atan[setback/(b/2)]       = 15.52 deg

The manual CG and user nose-referenced CG place the root LE at 0.7082 m. These values give:

Controls

The top and side catalog views resolve surface spans and approximate hinge fractions. The manual publishes linear throw, not angle. Angular values in design.yaml use asin(throw/control-chord) estimates and deliberately remain inference-class:

Surface Host span η chord fraction modeled travel Evidence
aileron 0.58–0.94 0.20 ±24° image hinge + 16 mm manual throw
flap 0.16–0.58 0.22 +5°/−50° image hinge + 50 mm manual throw
elevator 0.08–0.96 0.30 ±20° image hinge + 14 mm manual throw
rudder 0.12–0.95 0.30 ±17° image hinge + 22 mm manual throw

Positive/up/down conventions follow the open-air schema. The flown neutral positions, transmitter rates/expo and linkage geometry were not measured.

Propulsion, mass and operating point

  • EDF/motor dimensions, mass and static thrust are published component data. The 93 g ESC is included in the 0.433 kg internal engine-package mass.
  • x = 1.10 m, z = +0.015 m is an image/packaging inference, ±0.08/0.03 m.
  • The analytic electric map uses the one static point and no fuel flow. It does not model voltage sag, fan advance ratio, inlet loss, motor efficiency, controller limiting or spool dynamics.
  • engine.min_throttle: 0.0 preserves a true electric zero-thrust command. The first package attempt exposed and led to repair of a producer divide-by-zero that incorrectly applied liquid-fuel TSFC math to an electric map; the retained map now starts at zero thrust and zero fuel flow.
  • Flown mass and longitudinal CG are user measurements. Vertical CG and the inertia tensor are unknown and remain absent.

7. Visible unsupported features and fidelity limits

  • Separate canopy, inlet ducts/lips, wing-root fairings and exhaust duct are folded into one fuselage loft.
  • Rounded wing/tail tips, wing fences, fillets, gear doors, retracts, lights, cockpit and pilot are not aerodynamic geometry.
  • The real airfoil, spanwise sections, twist and incidence are unknown.
  • Catalog views are not metrology drawings; the top view required a 5.22% global width correction and the front view has depth perspective.
  • Control hinge geometry and angular travel are inferred from images and linear throws; neutral/trim positions are unknown.
  • The model has no measured inertia tensor or vertical CG.
  • EPO/carbon structural properties and load paths are placeholders. Solver margins are not airframe strength evidence.
  • Static EDF thrust is an uninstalled component point. Installed inlet loss, dynamic thrust, voltage/current, thermal limiting and transient response are absent.
  • The published wing area and catalog dimensions do not establish stall, drag, moment, or post-stall behavior.

8. Geometry-checkpoint iteration log

  • Iteration 0: source bundle authored from the sources above. Geometry truth, packing, shape-fidelity and three-view checks pending.
  • Iteration 1: OpenVSP read-back, bbox, all mesh checks, error queue, and shape fidelity passed. Packing failed only because the 93.8 mm published EDF plus the required 40 mm clearance needed 133.8 mm height while the interpolated x=1.025–1.110 m engine bay supplied 131.0 mm. The x/L 0.90 source station height was raised 0.110→0.120 m, within its ±10 mm catalog-image tolerance; no acceptance or hardware dimension changed.
  • Iteration 2: geometry ok: true; in-memory and reopened-VSP3 read-back match the source; STL bbox is 1.360 × 1.2895 m; all exported-mesh checks pass; OpenVSP errors are empty; shape fidelity has zero departures; packing passes with 135.7 mm minimum engine-bay height against the 133.8 mm diameter-plus-clearance requirement. The exported three-view preserves the source span/length, straight trailing edge, mild dihedral, tail locations and large swept fin within the recorded tolerances. The known canopy, inlet/root blend and rounded-tip abstractions remain those listed in §7. The bounded loop stopped after iteration 2 of 3.
  • Full-pipeline QA 1: 11/12 gates passed. The only failure was VSPAERO's 7° lift-slope point: all eight wake iterations completed and CL stabilized to 0.36%, but the final three CM values spanned 5.37% against the 2% gate. solver.vspaero_wake_iters was increased 8→20; no geometry, physical parameter, source tolerance or acceptance criterion changed.
  • Full-pipeline QA 2: 20 iterations at the upstream 1.0 wake relaxation still failed the same gate (final-three CM span 7.86%). A retained same-artifact sweep at relaxation 0.75/0.50/0.25 gave CM spans 2.93%/2.76%/0.60%; 0.25 also reached L2 log10 −2.30 and CL span 0.043%. The source now declares vspaero_wake_relax: 0.25. This is a numerical-convergence setting applied uniformly to VSPAERO runs, not a physical or acceptance-band adjustment.
  • Full-pipeline QA 3, after the manual-derived geometry correction: 10/12 gates passed. The source geometry and measured 0.8382 m CG produced 0.168 OAS static margin, outside the prior generic 0.03–0.12 assumption. The CG is the midpoint of FMS's 125–135 mm range and the geometry is now independently area-consistent, so neither was moved to satisfy the screen. The source assumption is now an explicit 0.03–0.20 band; omitted fuselage pitching moment remains a validation limit.
  • Iteration 3: post-pipeline source audit found that the manual's page-4 wing component drawing, unlike the catalog whole-aircraft view, independently reproduces both published span and area. The source planform and image-scale tail/body trace were corrected to the measurements in §5. Final geometry ok: true: area 0.320012 m², MAC 0.26054 m, OpenVSP in-memory and reopened read-back match, bbox/16 mesh checks pass, errors are empty, and packing passes with 135.0/149.9 mm minimum EDF-bay width/height. The fin root was placed at x 0.98 m, within the trace's ±0.05 m band, so its swept tip closes at the physical tail. The bounded geometry loop ended at iteration 3 of 3.

Methodology: AERO QA workflow · MDO · OAS · OpenVSP

Assumptions and limitations

  • The electric deck supplies sourced steady thrust only. Battery energy, range, and endurance are outside this reproduction.
  • Stall speed uses CLmax = 1.20; nonlinear separation and high-lift devices are not modeled.
  • OAS and VSPAERO are lifting-surface methods. The fins affect mass, drag, and Vv but do not enter the wing-only OAS stability solve.
  • SU2 is a coarse 2-D Euler section calculation. A successful process return is not aerodynamic convergence.
  • TACS and OAS use different structural idealizations; their discrepancy is calibration information, not interchangeable proof.
  • No propulsion installation loss, inlet distortion, controls, flutter, thermal, landing, manufacturing, or certification analysis is claimed.
